summary: Peshtigo Reef, a shoal in lower Green Bay, was marked by light vessel LV 77 from 1906 to 1934; the steel lighthouse on a crib and pier replaced it in 1936 and runs unattended under Coast Guard care.

lens.note: Original fourth-order lens; the 1990s work replaced the optic with a 300 mm automated acrylic lens (NRHP section 7, p. 7).

structures.note: About 30 ft (9.1 m) tower on the service building; the whole lighthouse, foundation base to lantern top, is about 80 ft (24.4 m) (NRHP section 7, pp. 1-2).

structures.type: steel scow-type light vessel, 110 tons, towed

access.note: Coast Guard aid to navigation on a crib and pier in open water. Tower closed; best seen from the water or the air (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Lighthouse Board team surveys Green Bay and names Peshtigo Reef among three priority places
Day beacon built on the reef: 30-foot square wooden crib with pyramidal tower and iron cage (NRHP gives 1869; LighthouseFriends quotes a Board description and says complete by June 1870)
Light vessel LV 77 first exhibits its lantern on station, 28 April 1906 (the record's 1906 first_lit belongs to this vessel, not to a lighthouse)
8-inch compressed-air chime whistle installed on LV 77; the vessel was off station 18 August to 16 September while it was fitted
Steamer Jupiter grounds on the reef in dense fog, late November 1914 (LighthouseFriends only)
Last navigation season of LV 77 on the reef
Temporary light and fog signal set atop the concrete pier, August 1935
Permanent lighthouse on a sheet-pile ring, crib filled and pier built; construction began September 1934
Permanent light in service: completed June 1936 (NRHP); placed in full commission 6 May 1936 (Commissioner's 1936 report, as quoted by LighthouseFriends)
Lighthouse replaces LV 77 as the reef's mark; the light vessel is discontinued
1990s: optic, fog signal and power supply replaced; generator removed after a solar array was installed
Fiscal 1919 table: light vessel rendered assistance to motor boat Wyandotte (five persons aboard) and provided a temporary rudder for steering to port; the table gives no date

wrecks.outcome: Grounded on Peshtigo Reef in dense fog, late November 1914, a few days after the light vessel was withdrawn for the season; bound Green Bay to Buffalo with 6,000 tons of coal. Source: LighthouseFriends only.
Light vessel rendered assistance and provided a temporary rudder for steering to port (Commissioner's table, fiscal 1919)

corrections.why: The 1905 build date and 1906 first light belong to light vessel LV 77, which marked the reef on station from 1906 to 1934. The lighthouse was built 1934-36 and first lit as a permanent light in 1936 (NRHP section 8, pp. 4-5; LighthouseFriends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1905 and 1906 dates are for light vessel LV 77, not for a lighthouse. Both the nomination and LighthouseFriends date the first exhibited light of the vessel to 28 April 1906 and the lighthouse to 1936.

notes_for_editor: Record correction: the built 1905 / first_lit 1906 entries are for light vessel LV 77; the lighthouse is 1936 (see corrections). Disagreements left open: (1) lamp strength: 20,000 cp (NRHP, 1936 description), 26,000 cp (LighthouseFriends), 2,000 cp and 11 miles (Bulletin 1935 notice); the nomination's 16 miles (1936) versus 9 miles (today). (2) Completion: June 1936 (NRHP) versus 6 May 1936 (Commissioner's 1936 report as quoted by LighthouseFriends); the 1936 Bulletin says only 'this season'. (3) Day beacon: NRHP says appropriation withdrawn in 1867 and beacon built 1869; LighthouseFriends says $10,000 remained and the beacon was complete by June 1870. The Commissioner's 1936 and 1923 reports and the 1902-1905 Board reports are not in the local corpus; a check against them would settle (1)-(3). The Commissioner's table at scan p. 463 (printed p. 63) is the FISCAL 1919 table, not 1917 as the first draft said; the page image was read and confirms the heading and the row: 'Peshtigo Reef Light Vessel No. 77, Wis.' | motor boat Wyandotte | 'Rendered assistance to boat with 5 persons aboard and provided temporary rudder for steering to port.' The row was matched by its position on the page image; the date is not given in the table. The 1917 Bulletin p. 19 notice (OCR) moves Reinhart Larsen from master of LV 77 to mate of Grays Reef LV 57; it conflicts with the p. 20 resignation. The story states the conflict and follows the resignation (source 16). The 1914 grounding of the steamer Jupiter rests on LighthouseFriends alone; the Bulletin volumes in the corpus show only tender Jupiter entries for 1912-1917. Conrad Stram: the USLHS roster for us-wi-sturgeon-bay-canal lists Conrad A. Stram as head keeper 1927-1933, and LighthouseFriends places a Stram at the Sturgeon Bay Canal Lighthouse; no link is made here (no person slug, no other_stations) because the Peshtigo stint comes only from LighthouseFriends. The USLHS place record for Peshtigo Reef (archives.uslhs.org/places/peshtigo-reef-0) lists no roster. The record's 2007 NRHP listing year is not visible in the nomination text in our copy. One Chronicling America search for Wisconsin newspapers 1905-1940 found nothing usable. The 1990s dating of the equipment changes is approximate ('during the 1990s'). Wikipedia was not used as a source. Also checked this pass: the 1935 notice on the 72-foot light is on PDF p. 22 (printed p. 218), not p. 21. The 1916 Bulletin p. 12 (OCR) lists 'Richard D. Baxter' moved to mate of 'Peshtigo Reef Light Vessel No. 71' (number likely wrong for 77, since LV 71 was Diamond Shoal, N.C.); not used. The range was 9 miles with no unit in the nomination, so range_nm (7.8, a statute-to-nautical conversion) was removed rather than kept. Tower height 24.4 m was the whole lighthouse; the tower alone is about 30 ft (9.1 m). Wording pass: about 18 sentences were reworded where they followed NRHP or LighthouseFriends wording closely, and the three LighthouseFriends quotations (1898 Board, 1923 Commissioner, 1936 commission date) were turned into paraphrase, leaving one short quotation per copyrighted source at most.
